tips.title: After the noun is the default
tips.body: *Un film **intéressant**, une voiture **rouge**, un garçon **anglais**.* Most French adjectives follow the noun — colours, nationalities, and almost every adjective of more than two syllables. If in doubt, put it after.

tips.title: BAGS go before
tips.body: **B**eauty, **A**ge, **G**oodness, **S**ize: *beau, joli, jeune, vieux, nouveau, bon, mauvais, grand, petit, gros, long*. *Un **petit** chien, une **jolie** maison, un **bon** ami, un **vieux** livre.* The short, common ones go first.

tips.title: Bel, nouvel, vieil before a vowel
tips.body: *Un **bel** homme, un **nouvel** ami, un **vieil** arbre.* *Beau, nouveau* and *vieux* have a special masculine form before a vowel or silent *h*, so the words run together. The feminine forms — *belle, nouvelle, vieille* — sound the same.

tips.title: Des becomes de before a preceding adjective
tips.body: *J'ai **de** bons amis. Il y a **de** petites maisons.* When a plural adjective goes **before** the noun, *des* shrinks to **de**. *Des amis sympas* keeps *des* because *sympas* follows.

tips.title: Position can change meaning
tips.body: *Un **ancien** élève* — a former pupil; *un bâtiment **ancien*** — an old building. *Ma **propre** chambre* — my own room; *une chambre **propre*** — a clean room. A few adjectives mean different things before and after, and *ancien* and *propre* are the ones GCSE texts use.

steps.title: Après le nom
steps.body:
In English the adjective comes first: *a red car*. In French, **most adjectives follow the noun**: *une voiture **rouge***.

**After the noun** — the default:

- colours: *un pull **bleu**, des chaussures **noires***
- nationalities: *un ami **français**, une ville **anglaise***
- shape and description: *une table **ronde**, un film **intéressant**, une matière **difficile**, un prof **sympa***
- participles used as adjectives: *un enfant **fatigué**, une rue **animée***

The adjective still **agrees** wherever it sits: *des chaussures noires, une ville anglaise*.

**Two adjectives after the noun** are joined by *et*: *un film long et ennuyeux*.

**With c'est**: *c'est une émission intéressante* — the adjective goes after *émission*, and agrees with it.

steps.title: Avant le nom : BAGS
steps.body:
A small group of short, common adjectives goes **before** the noun. Remember them as **BAGS**:

- **B**eauty: *beau / belle, joli(e)*
- **A**ge: *jeune, vieux / vieille, nouveau / nouvelle*
- **G**oodness: *bon / bonne, mauvais(e)*
- **S**ize: *grand(e), petit(e), gros / grosse, long / longue*

*Un **petit** village, une **grande** maison, un **bon** repas, une **jolie** fille, un **vieux** château, un **jeune** homme, un **nouveau** portable, un **long** voyage.*

**Irregular forms**: *beau, nouveau* and *vieux* change before a **masculine noun starting with a vowel or silent h**:

- *un **beau** garçon* → *un **bel** homme*
- *un **nouveau** prof* → *un **nouvel** élève*
- *un **vieux** livre* → *un **vieil** ami*

Their plurals: *beaux, nouveaux, vieux* (no extra *-s*); feminine: *belle(s), nouvelle(s), vieille(s)*.

**Des → de before a plural adjective**: *j'ai **de** bons amis*, *il y a **de** jolies maisons*, but *des maisons modernes*.

**Mixing**: a BAGS adjective before and another after: *un **petit** chien **noir**, une **jolie** robe **rouge**, un **vieux** film **français***.

steps.title: Les cas particuliers
steps.body:
**Adjectives that change meaning with position**:

- *un **ancien** élève* (a former pupil) — *un bâtiment **ancien*** (an old building)
- *ma **propre** chambre* (my own room) — *une chambre **propre*** (a clean room)
- *un **grand** homme* (a great man) — *un homme **grand*** (a tall man)
- *un **pauvre** garçon* (a poor — unlucky — boy) — *un garçon **pauvre*** (a boy with no money)
- *le **dernier** jour* (the last / final day) — *la semaine **dernière*** (last week — the one just gone)
- *le **prochain** train* (the next train) — *la semaine **prochaine*** (next week)

***Dernier* and *prochain*** are the two you use constantly: **before** for last / next in a series, **after** for time expressions — *la semaine dernière, l'année prochaine*.

**Comparatives always follow**: *une maison plus grande*, *un film moins intéressant* — even for BAGS adjectives.

**Numbers and quantities go first**: *les deux premiers jours*, *trois jolies photos*.

**Premier / première** goes before: *le premier étage, la première fois*.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.body:
**Part A.**

1. Put the adjective in the right place: *une maison (grand), un pull (rouge), un ami (bon), une ville (anglais)*.
2. List the BAGS adjectives from memory.
3. Write *a handsome man, a new friend, an old tree* with the special forms.

**Part B.**

4. Write three noun phrases with one adjective before and one after.
5. Write *I have good friends* and *there are pretty houses*, with *de*.
6. Write *last week* and *the last day* — which *dernier* goes where?

**Part C.**

7. Explain the difference between *un ancien élève* and *un bâtiment ancien*.
8. Write a comparison with a BAGS adjective, e.g. *a bigger house*.
9. Describe your house or flat in six sentences, using at least four BAGS adjectives and four adjectives after the noun.

For question 9, check every *des* before a preceding plural adjective.

steps.title: Going deeper
steps.body:
**Default after, BAGS before.** Any adjective you are not sure about goes after — that rule is right far more often than it is wrong.

**Use the vowel forms.** *Un bel appartement, un nouvel ami, un vieil homme.* They are a visible sign of control, and each is a chance an examiner notices.

**Shrink des to de.** *De bons amis, de jolies fleurs, de grandes fenêtres.* Missed by most students; correct in a top answer.

**Stack both positions.** *Un petit chien noir, une jolie robe bleue, un vieux film français.* A noun with an adjective either side reads as fluent.

**Know dernier and prochain.** *La semaine dernière* (last week) but *le dernier jour* (the final day); *l'année prochaine* but *le prochain bus*. You use these in every tense-range sentence.

**Exploit the meaning changes.** *Mon ancien collège, ma propre chambre* — a former school and a room of your own are things you actually write about.

**Comparatives after, always.** *Une maison plus grande*, never *une plus grande maison* — though *la plus grande maison* (the biggest house) as a superlative can go before.

**Agree first, place second.** Position never removes agreement: *de belles maisons anciennes* — both agree with *maisons*.

steps.title: Summary
steps.body:
- **Most adjectives follow the noun**: colours, nationalities, descriptions, participles.
- **BAGS go before**: *beau, joli, jeune, vieux, nouveau, bon, mauvais, grand, petit, gros, long*.
- **Vowel forms**: *bel, nouvel, vieil* before a masculine noun starting with a vowel or silent *h*.
- Plurals: *beaux, nouveaux, vieux*; feminine: *belle, nouvelle, vieille*.
- **Des → de** before a preceding plural adjective: *de bons amis*.
- Both positions together: *un petit chien noir*.
- Two after the noun: joined by *et*.
- **Meaning changes**: *ancien* (former / old), *propre* (own / clean), *grand* (great / tall), *dernier* (final / last), *prochain* (next in series / next week).
- *La semaine dernière, l'année prochaine* — time expressions take the adjective **after**.
- **Comparatives follow** the noun: *une maison plus grande*.
- *Premier* and numbers go before.
- Agreement applies in both positions.

questions.solution: **My former maths teacher.** *Ancien* before the noun = former.
*Propre* **after** the noun = clean. Before the noun it means *own*: *ma propre chambre*.

questions.prompt: Why is it **un nouvel ami** but **une nouvelle amie**?
options: Nouvel is the masculine form before a vowel; nouvelle is the feminine
Nouvel is a spelling variant used only in writing
Nouvelle is used before vowels and nouvel elsewhere
Ami is masculine plural, so nouveau loses its ending
questions.solution: *Nouveau* has a special **masculine** form, *nouvel*, before a vowel. *Amie* is feminine, so it takes the ordinary feminine *nouvelle*. They sound identical.

examTechnique.body:
Put adjectives **after** the noun unless they are **BAGS** — beauty, age, goodness, size — which go before. Use **bel, nouvel, vieil** before a masculine vowel, shrink **des to de** before a preceding plural adjective, and keep agreement in both positions.

Know *dernier* and *prochain* in both positions, use *propre* and *ancien* for their before-the-noun meanings, and keep comparatives after the noun.
examinerErrors: La dernière semaine for last week.
Forgetting agreement on an adjective before the noun.
Ma chambre propre for my own room.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 answer places every adjective by the rule — colours and descriptions after, BAGS before — with full agreement, uses *bel / nouvel / vieil* where a vowel follows, and writes *de bons amis* rather than *des*. It stacks an adjective either side of a noun, distinguishes *la semaine dernière* from *le dernier jour*, uses *propre* or *ancien* for their before-the-noun meaning, and keeps comparatives after the noun.
